settings.headline: Numbing cream FAQ
settings.subhead: Honest answers to the questions people ask most about cosmetic numbing — what it does, how to use it safely, and when to check with your practitioner.
settings.image_alt: Editorial Senseless topical preparation range on a warm off-white background

settings.body: Every page on Senseless includes guidance relevant to that product or topic. This page brings together the questions we’re asked most often about shipping, products, application, safety, trade accounts and orders.

settings.question: Where is my order?
settings.answer: You’ll receive an email containing your Royal Mail tracking number as soon as your order has been dispatched. If you can’t find it, please check your junk or spam folder. You can also track your parcel using the Royal Mail tracking service.

settings.question: Royal Mail says my order has been delivered, but I can’t find it.
settings.answer:
Our parcels are designed to fit through a standard letterbox whenever possible. Please check with anyone else at the property and any safe places where the parcel may have been left.

If you’re still unable to locate it, contact us at cs@senseless.uk and we’ll investigate with Royal Mail.

settings.question: Is my order shipped in discreet packaging?
settings.answer: Yes. Every order is dispatched in plain, unbranded packaging for complete discretion.

settings.question: Is Senseless designed for professional treatments?
settings.answer:
Yes. Senseless was developed for the people who work on skin. The range is designed for use before procedures such as tattooing, piercings, injectables, microneedling, laser treatments, skin rejuvenation, permanent makeup (SPMU) and waxing.

Many studios and clinics also retail Senseless directly to clients preparing for their appointments.

settings.question: Which strength should I choose?
settings.answer: Senseless is available in multiple strengths because different treatments and clients have different requirements. Our recommendation system will guide you to the most appropriate option based on your planned procedure. If you’re unsure, contact our team before ordering and we’ll happily advise.

settings.question: Can I use Senseless alongside another numbing cream?
settings.answer: No. We do not recommend combining multiple topical numbing products. Using more than one product increases the likelihood of skin irritation and makes it difficult to identify the cause of any reaction. For best results, use Senseless on its own and follow the application instructions.

settings.question: Does alcohol or caffeine affect performance?
settings.answer: They can. Many practitioners recommend avoiding alcohol and limiting caffeine for at least 24 hours before treatment, as both may reduce the perceived effectiveness of topical numbing products.

settings.question: Why didn’t it work as well as I expected?
settings.answer:
The most common reasons include:

  • Applying too little product.
  • Not leaving it on long enough.
  • Failing to cover it where recommended.
  • Individual skin differences.
  • The type of procedure being performed.

If you feel your experience wasn’t as expected, contact cs@senseless.uk and we’ll help identify what may have affected the result.

settings.question: Are Senseless products compliant?
settings.answer: Yes. Every Senseless product complies with UK cosmetic legislation and is supported by its own Cosmetic Product Safety Report (CPSR) completed by an independent qualified safety assessor.

settings.question: How do I apply Senseless correctly?
settings.answer: Clean and thoroughly dry the treatment area. Apply a thick, even layer across the entire area to be treated. Cover with occlusive film (such as cling film) where recommended to improve absorption. Leave for approximately 45–60 minutes before your procedure unless your practitioner advises otherwise. Full instructions are available on our How to Apply page.

settings.question: How much should I apply?
settings.answer: Apply a generous, clearly visible layer over the complete treatment area. Using too little product is one of the most common reasons for reduced performance.

settings.question: How long does it take to work?
settings.answer: Most users begin noticing the effects after approximately 30–45 minutes, with optimal comfort typically achieved after around 45–60 minutes when applied correctly.

settings.question: How long does the effect last?
settings.answer: Individual experiences vary, but customer feedback suggests comfort typically lasts between one and three hours, depending on the product used, application method, skin type and treatment.

settings.question: Can I use Senseless before anti-wrinkle injections or dermal fillers?
settings.answer: Yes. Many practitioners recommend Senseless before injectable treatments to help improve comfort throughout the procedure. Always follow the advice of your treating practitioner.

settings.question: Is Senseless suitable for microneedling?
settings.answer: Yes. Microneedling is one of the most common procedures Senseless is used before, both in clinics and by trained practitioners.

settings.question: Can I use Senseless before laser treatments?
settings.answer: Yes. Senseless is commonly used before laser procedures, including laser hair removal and various skin rejuvenation treatments.

settings.question: Is it suitable before permanent makeup (SPMU)?
settings.answer: Yes. Many SPMU artists use Senseless to help improve client comfort during longer procedures.

settings.question: Do I need to perform a patch test?
settings.answer: Yes. Before your first use, carry out a patch test at least 24 hours beforehand. Apply a small amount to the inside of your wrist or elbow and leave it for 24 hours. If irritation occurs, do not continue with full application.

settings.question: Can I use Senseless during pregnancy?
settings.answer: Speak to your GP, midwife or healthcare professional before using any topical numbing product during pregnancy. Do not use without appropriate medical advice.

settings.question: Is Senseless suitable for sensitive skin?
settings.answer: If you have sensitive skin, a patch test is particularly important. If redness, itching or irritation develops during the patch test, discontinue use. Anyone with an existing skin condition should seek medical advice before use.

settings.question: What should I do if I experience a reaction?
settings.answer: Stop using the product immediately and wash the area thoroughly with clean water. If symptoms persist or worsen, seek medical advice. Do not use the product again until advised by a healthcare professional.

settings.question: Can I apply Senseless to broken or irritated skin?
settings.answer: No. Do not apply Senseless to broken, inflamed, infected or sunburnt skin. This warning appears on every product label and should always be followed.

settings.question: Is there a minimum order?
settings.answer: No. There is no minimum order value for most trade accounts, although larger volume discounts are available as your purchasing increases.

settings.question: Can I return my order?
settings.answer: Yes. You have 30 days from receiving your order to request a return. Products must be unopened, unused and returned in their original packaging. Contact cs@senseless.uk with your order number and we’ll guide you through the returns process.

settings.question: How quickly do you dispatch orders?
settings.answer: Orders placed before our published daily dispatch cut-off are normally dispatched the same working day. Delivery times depend on the shipping option selected at checkout.

settings.question: Is Senseless suitable before a tattoo?
settings.answer:
Yes. A tattoo sitting is usually the longest appointment the range is used before, so the length of the booking — rather than the size of the design — is what the strength is matched to. Cream is the general-purpose choice, gel suits smaller defined work, and spray covers a broad area such as a limb or a back piece.

Ask your artist before you book. Studios differ, some apply their own, and a few would rather you didn't use anything at all — their answer settles it.

settings.question: What should I tell my tattoo artist?
settings.answer:
Tell them at booking rather than on the day: that you're considering a topical preparation beforehand, and would they rather you did or didn't. If they say yes, ask whether they want it applied at a particular time, and mention it again briefly when you arrive.

Expect the area to be cleaned again before the stencil goes on — your artist needs a completely clear surface to work from.

settings.question: Is Senseless suitable before a piercing?
settings.answer:
It can be, though we'd rather be straight with you: a standard lobe piercing is over in seconds and most people don't need anything. Where it earns its place is cartilage, several piercings in one appointment, or simply wanting to arrive calmer than last time. Gel is usually the format, since a piercing site is small and precise.

Ask your piercer first — studios have their own protocols around a site that has to be marked and cleaned before it's pierced.

settings.question: Can I use Senseless on a healing tattoo or a fresh piercing?
settings.answer:
No. Senseless is applied to clean, unbroken skin before an appointment. Fresh tattoo work and a new piercing are broken skin, and the numbing range is not for use on them.

For looking after skin afterwards, follow the aftercare instructions your artist or piercer gave you — theirs come first.

settings.body:
• Senseless is a UK cosmetic numbing range, formulated in the United Kingdom.
  • Numbing is a cosmetic preparation, not an anaesthetic.
  • Apply only to clean, healthy skin, patch test, and follow the product's instructions.
  • Many practitioners apply their own numbing, so check before your appointment.
